questions.question: You are driving on a rural gravel road and see a triangular warning sign indicating a motor gate ahead. The road appears clear and there are no visible animals nearby. What is the correct and safest driving response?

options.text: Maintain your speed, as the gate is built for vehicles to drive over without stopping.
Accelerate slightly to reduce the time spent driving over the grid surface.
Slow down before reaching the motor gate, maintain firm control of the steering wheel, and proceed cautiously.
Stop completely and wait to be waved through by a farm official.

questions.question: While driving on a highway, you see a triangular warning sign indicating a tunnel ahead. The tunnel entrance is not yet visible. What are the correct precautions you should take as you approach and enter the tunnel?

options.text: Maintain your speed and turn on your high beam headlights to see clearly inside the tunnel.
Reduce your speed, switch on your dipped headlights or fog lights if necessary, and avoid overtaking inside the tunnel.
Stop before entering the tunnel to check for any height or width restrictions.
Turn off your vehicle’s headlights inside the tunnel to save battery power.

questions.question: You are driving a delivery truck with a height of 4.5 meters and see a triangular warning sign indicating a height restriction of 4.42 meters ahead. The actual height barrier is not yet visible. What is the correct course of action?

options.text: Continue driving; the warning sign is just advisory, and you can proceed if the truck fits under the barrier.
Immediately stop and find an alternative route before reaching the height restriction.
Slow down and carefully proceed, trusting that your truck can clear the height restriction carefully.
Attempt to drive through quickly before any height barrier appears to avoid traffic buildup.

questions.question: You are driving a vehicle that is 2.3 meters wide and approach a road showing a triangular warning sign indicating a width restriction of 2.1 meters ahead. The restriction is not yet visible. What should you do?

options.text: Continue driving carefully and try to squeeze through the narrow section.
Slow down and prepare to stop and find an alternate route that accommodates your vehicle's width.
Signal to oncoming traffic and proceed if there is no immediate traffic.
Attempt to pass by driving as close to the edge as possible to avoid damage.

questions.question: You are driving a truck that is 16 meters long and approach a triangular warning sign indicating a length restriction of 15 meters ahead. The restriction barrier is not yet visible. What should you do?

options.text: Continue driving carefully and try to navigate the restricted section slowly.
Stop immediately and find an alternative route that accommodates your vehicle length.
Reduce speed and proceed, assuming the restriction only applies to parked vehicles.
Signal to other drivers and attempt to reverse if the passage is too narrow.

questions.question: You are driving a heavy goods vehicle downhill and see a triangular warning sign indicating a steep descent ahead. What is the safest and most legally appropriate action to take?

options.text: Maintain your current speed and rely on the vehicle's regular brakes throughout the descent.
Shift to a lower gear before starting the descent and control your speed using engine braking.
Increase speed to maintain momentum while descending.
Use the parking brake intermittently during the descent to slow down.

questions.question: While driving a heavy vehicle, you approach a triangular warning sign indicating a steep ascent. What is the safest and most efficient driving technique to manage this section?

options.text: Maintain your current gear and increase the accelerator pressure to climb faster.
Shift to a lower gear before the ascent and maintain steady throttle to prevent stalling.
Use the clutch to slip frequently to gain more torque while ascending.
Shift to a higher gear immediately at the base of the hill to conserve fuel.

questions.question: While driving on a two lane highway, you see a triangular warning sign indicating a slow moving heavy vehicle ahead. The road is slightly winding, and there is oncoming traffic. What is the best and safest course of action?

options.text: Attempt to overtake immediately before the next bend to avoid delay.
Reduce your speed, maintain a safe following distance, and only overtake when it is clearly safe and legal.
Maintain your speed and follow closely behind to reduce overtaking distance.
Sound your horn continuously to encourage the heavy vehicle to move faster.

questions.question: You are driving on a paved road and see a triangular warning sign indicating that a gravel road begins ahead. What is the best driving approach to ensure safety?

options.text: Maintain your current speed since the road surface change does not affect vehicle handling.
Reduce your speed gradually before the gravel section and be prepared for reduced traction and longer stopping distances.
Accelerate quickly to cross the gravel section before loose stones can affect your vehicle.
Immediately stop and inspect your vehicle's tires before proceeding.

questions.question: You have been driving cautiously on a gravel road and see a triangular warning sign indicating that the gravel road ends ahead. What should you anticipate and do as you approach this sign?

options.text: Increase your speed immediately, as the road will become smoother and safer.
Maintain your current cautious speed, then prepare to adjust your driving as the road surface transitions to tar or concrete.
Expect the road surface to become less stable and reduce speed further later.
Stop completely and check your tires before continuing.
